**Finding: LICENSE — compliant (no redline proposed).**

The agreement contains no vendor-to-customer licence grant, because SFJ does not license IP to us at all — we hold ownership:

- **11.1.1.1(a)** — PB remains sole and exclusive owner of all Existing PB Intellectual Property and of PB IP arising independently.
- **11.1.1.3(a)** — PB is the exclusive and sole owner of all Trial Inventions regardless of inventorship, with SFJ assigning and causing its affiliates/Permitted Third Parties to assign.
- **11.1.1.4** — PB acquires sole and exclusive ownership, even as to SFJ, of the Trial Data Package including all Research Results.
- **15.15** — all rights not exclusively granted to SFJ are reserved to "PB and its Affiliates"; no PB IP is licensed to SFJ except under the Program Transfer Agreement.
- **15.6** — either Party may assign, sublicense or transfer the Agreement and all rights to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger/stock/asset sale, satisfying the successor-transfer element without consent.

Nothing in the document is revocable at SFJ's discretion (the word "revocable" appears nowhere), and no clause excludes our affiliates or contractors. Ownership subsumes the preferred checklist, so the rule sits above the preferred position and should not be redlined. Noted only in the rationale (not as a deviation): SFJ holds the Trial Data Package until the purchase trigger, but Research Results are deemed PB's Confidential Information with PB as disclosing Party, so our interim use is unrestricted.
